docs.title: Yakcov
docs.text:
Yet Another Kotlin COmpose Validation library.

Yakcov makes TextField (and any other input) validation painless in Compose Multiplatform. Validators are backed by Compose snapshot state, so your UI reacts automatically; validation outcomes are severity-ranked (ERROR, WARNING, INFO, SUCCESS); and the same rules run on Android, JVM, JS, Wasm, and iOS.

These docs can't lie

Every code block on this site is pulled from the docs-examples module, which compiles in CI against the current library API. If an example here stopped working, the build would fail before the docs could ship.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Yakcov publishes all targets to Maven Central — add the common artifact and Gradle resolves the right target per platform:

commonMain {
    dependencies {
        implementation("com.chrisjenx.yakcov:library:${version}")
    }
}

docs.title: Yakcov in 30 seconds
docs.text:
@Composable
fun BasicSignUpScreen(onSubmit: (email: String, password: String) -> Unit) {
    // No state holder: the validators live in the composable, remembered across
    // recompositions. Each one owns a TextFieldState (the field's text) and validates it by
    // observing the state — there is no onValueChange to wire.
    val email = rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules = listOf(Required, Email))
    val password = rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules = listOf(Required, MinLength(8)))

    Column {
        with(email) {
            OutlinedTextField(
                state = textFieldState,
                label = { Text("Email") },
                isError = isError(),
                supportingText = supportingText(),
                lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .fillMaxWidth()
                    // Show errors when focus leaves the field; shake on invalid submit.
                    .validationConfig(validateOnFocusLost = true, shakeOnInvalid = true),
            )
        }
        with(password) {
            OutlinedTextField(
                state = textFieldState,
                label = { Text("Password") },
                isError = isError(),
                supportingText = supportingText(),
                lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .fillMaxWidth()
                    .validationConfig(validateOnFocusLost = true, shakeOnInvalid = true),
            )
        }
        Button(
            onClick = {
                // Form-level validate(): surfaces errors on every field, true when all pass.
                if (listOf(email, password).validate()) {
                    onSubmit(email.value, password.value)
                }
            },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        ) { Text("Create account") }
    }
}

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Getting started — rules, error display, validationConfig, form-level submit
  • Pattern guides, each showing all the layers (UI, state holder, validation wiring):
    • Basic screen — no state holder
    • ViewModel — validator owned by the ViewModel
    • MVI / UDF — pure reducer, immutable model
    • Circuit — validator owned by the presenter
  • Recipes: custom rules, phone validation

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Validation is composed from ValueValidatorRules. Built-ins cover the common cases — Required, Email, MinLength(n), MaxLength(n), Phone(region) (see phone validation), HexColor, OneOf(allowed), typed numeric Min/Max/InRange, and more in com.chrisjenx.yakcov.strings / com.chrisjenx.yakcov.generic.

Apply any rule conditionally with onlyWhen: Required.onlyWhen(isBusiness) runs the rule only while the flag is true and passes otherwise.

ValueValidatorRule is a fun interface, so one-off rules are a lambda away:

// ValueValidatorRule is a fun interface — one-off rules can be inline SAM lambdas.
// Severity is graded: error/warning/info/success all flow through supportingText.
val NoPlusAddressing = ValueValidatorRule<String> { value ->
    if ("+" in value) RegularValidationResult.warning("Plus-addressing may break receipts")
    else RegularValidationResult.success()
}

See the built-in rules reference for the full catalog, and custom rules for reusable rule types and severity grading.

docs.title: Two validator families
docs.text:
In-composition State-holder-owned (headless) Create with rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules) (the field owns a TextFieldState) / rememberGenericValueValidator(state, rules) FieldValidator(initial, rules): plain constructor Choose when The form has no state holder; everything lives in the composable A ViewModel/presenter owns form state; you want submit() testable without UI

Both are snapshot-state backed, so composables that read them recompose automatically. The pattern guides (ViewModel, MVI, Circuit) show which to reach for in each architecture. For a reducer form whose fields own a TextFieldState, follow the MVI/UDF setup.

docs.title: Showing errors
docs.text:
Validation severity and error display are separate channels: rules compute a severity on every change, but nothing is shown until the validator decides errors should be visible (focus lost, submit, …). That's why nothing flashes red while the user is still typing.

  • isError() / FieldValidationState.isError — true once errors are shown and severity is ERROR
  • supportingText() — a ready-made slot value for Material TextFields; renders the most severe message, or null when nothing should show. Pass supportingText(default = "…") to show a plain hint while the field has no message (e.g. a pristine field); the same default works on FieldValidationState.text()/supportingText()
  • Outcome severities: ERROR > WARNING > INFO > SUCCESS. Warnings and info messages flow through the same display channel without blocking submission.

docs.title: validationConfig
docs.text:
For in-composition validators, the validationConfig modifier wires interaction behavior:

modifier = Modifier.validationConfig(
    validateOnFocusLost = true,       // start validating when focus leaves the field
    shakeOnInvalid = true,            // shake the field when validate() fails
    showErrorOnInteraction = false,   // defer isError until validate() is called
)

For headless FieldValidators there is no validationConfig modifier. Validate on focus loss by calling field.onFocusLost() from Modifier.onFocusLost { ... }. For shake, pass FieldValidator.attempts as the shakeTrigger of Modifier.validationBehavior(isError, shakeTrigger, onFocusLost), or use Modifier.shakeOnInvalid(isError, trigger) directly. Error display stays yours to gate, via the showError flag you thread through toFieldState.

docs.title: Form-level submit
docs.text:
Validate everything at once; errors surface on every field and the call tells you whether to proceed:

if (listOf(email, password).validate()) { /* all valid — submit */ }

Works on both families: List<ValueValidator<*, *>>.validate() and List<FieldValidator<*>>.validate().

docs.title: Decision record: TextFieldState support
docs.text:
Status: accepted · Since: the release after 1.12.1 / 1.13.0-alpha01 · Scope: additive on every channel, plus deprecations in the Compose 1.13+ artifacts

Compose is moving editable text from the value + onValueChange pair (String / TextFieldValue, VisualTransformation) to a field-owned TextFieldState with InputTransformation / OutputTransformation for formatting. yakcov supports both side by side: every TextFieldValue API keeps working, and both kinds mix in one validate(), so an app can migrate one field or module at a time. In the Compose 1.13+ artifacts the value/onValueChange wrappers are @Deprecated (warning level), matching Compose itself; see Deprecation.

docs.title: Why: text that round-trips through a model loses input
docs.text:
With value + onValueChange, the field renders whatever the model holds. If the model updates later than the next key arrives (a store hop, a reducer on another dispatcher, a slow frame), every late write resets the field's edit buffer to stale text. Keystrokes are lost and a mid-text paste lands in the wrong place. A TextFieldState field owns its text on the Compose clock, and the model only observes it. Nothing writes the model back into the field while the user types.

Both fields get the same keystroke on the same frame, every 10 ms, and feed the same model that applies each change 16 ms late. Rendered on the JVM with Compose's desktop runtime by SkippedInputDemoRender (regenerate with YAKCOV_DEMO_OUT=/tmp/demo ./gradlew :library:jvmTest --tests '*SkippedInputDemoRender*' --rerun).

Measured with the same keystrokes and the same async model (each change reduced 16 ms late):

Run Legacy TextFieldValue hoist TextFieldState + textChanges() JVM UI test, 19 chars at 10 ms gaps (AsyncModelInputTest) teqikbonfx (9/19 kept) exact Android emulator, adb input text (43 chars), run 1 qikbrwn fjm e t laog exact Android emulator, run 2 the quick brop azog exact Mid-text paste / caret edit lands wrong (test control) lands at the caret, caret preserved

The demo is SkippedInputActivity in :sample (it has a model-lag slider): adb shell am start -n com.chrisjenx.yakcov.sample/.SkippedInputActivity.

The rule this record follows throughout: the TextFieldState is the only writer of a field's text while the user is typing. The model is downstream of it, and the only model → field write is an explicit, one-shot re-seed (§4).

docs.title: What ships
docs.text:
API Purpose TextFieldStateValidator / rememberTextFieldStateValidator Validator-owns-state over a TextFieldState. Same rules, members and error timing as TextFieldValueValidator. Modifier.onFocusCursorToEnd(state: TextFieldState, highlight) Caret to end (or select all) on focus, through the state's own selection. The validator has the same member. TextFieldState.textChanges(): Flow<String> The state → Model hand-off for reducer (UDF) forms. Emits text only, never caret moves. validationBehavior, shakeOnInvalid, onFocusLost, validationConfig(validator) Unchanged. They never took a value, so they already work with TextFieldState fields.

TextFieldStateValidator extends ValueValidator<String, String>, so it mixes with TextFieldValueValidator in one listOf(a, b).validate() and keeps isValid, isError(), supportingText(), validate(), reset() and the validationConfig member exactly as before.

Works on every channel

TextFieldState and its material3 overloads exist on every Compose version yakcov builds (1.12.x stable and the 1.13 pre-release line), so the new API ships on both channels. You do not have to move to Compose 1.13 to start migrating.

docs.title: 1. Validator-owns-state
docs.text:
@Composable
fun EmailField() {
    // Owns a saveable TextFieldState and observes it — no onValueChange anywhere.
    val email = rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules = listOf(Required, Email))
    Column {
        with(email) {
            OutlinedTextField(
                state = textFieldState,
                label = { Text("Email") },
                modifier = Modifier
                    .onFocusCursorToEnd()
                    .validationConfig(
                        validateOnFocusLost = true,
                        shakeOnInvalid = true,
                        showErrorOnInteraction = false, // errors on blur/submit only
                    ),
                isError = isError(),
                supportingText = supportingText(),
            )
        }
        Button(onClick = { if (listOf(email).validate()) { /* submit */ } }) { Text("Save") }
    }
}

How validation observes the state. Rules read textFieldState.text through a snapshot read, so isValid/isError()/supportingText() recompute on every edit with no onValueChange. The one thing that needs a running observer is the move from pristine to validating on the user's first edit. That is the step onValueChange performs today, and it is what makes showErrorOnInteraction meaningful. observeTextChanges() does it with snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }. rememberTextFieldStateValidator and the validationConfig modifier both run it while the field is composed. A validator you construct yourself (for example as a val on a component) and use without validationConfig must run it: LaunchedEffect(v) { v.observeTextChanges() }, or launch it from the component's scope.

Error timing is unchanged. Errors show on blur (validateOnFocusLost = true) or submit (validate()). With showErrorOnInteraction = false they never show while a fresh field is being typed into, and after the first blur they update live. initialValidate = true still starts validating immediately, which a field whose starting value is already valid needs (an optional Email, a quantity seeded "1"). A pristine field still reports isValid == false.

docs.title: 2. Modifiers, and who owns the behaviour
docs.text:
validationBehavior(isError, shakeTrigger, onFocusLost) and shakeOnInvalid(isError, trigger) are already value-agnostic, so no TextFieldState overload is needed. The only value-coupled modifier was onFocusCursorToEnd, which now has a TextFieldState overload that edits the selection in place (placeCursorAtEnd() / selectAll()). There is no value to hoist and no callback to call.

Recommendation for a field wrapper (for example one AppTextField(state, rules, format, style)): the wrapper should own these behaviours and apply the yakcov modifiers internally, rather than asking every call site to chain them. Focus-loss validation, shake on invalid submit and caret-to-end are properties of "a validated field", not of a screen, and putting them in one place removes the per-call-site drift. The modifiers stay public as the building blocks, and keeping them small is what makes them composable in a wrapper.

docs.title: 3. UDF forms: what does the Model hold?
docs.text:
The options when the field owns a TextFieldState:

Option Verdict a. The TextFieldState itself in the Model ✗ It is a mutable, reference-identity holder, the same reason a Model never holds validators. copy() aliases it, == becomes identity, and persistence and time-travel break. b. An immutable String snapshot, kept in sync one way (state → Model) ✓ Recommended. The reducer is unchanged in shape. c. An adapter that computes FieldValidationState outside the reducer ✗ Validation moves out of reduce(), and showError gets two owners. textChanges() is the only adapter worth having: a one-liner that gets the toString()/selection detail right.

The component (Decompose component, ViewModel, presenter) owns the TextFieldState as a val next to its store. The Model holds the text as a String plus the field's FieldValidationState. The reducer folds rules exactly as today.

private val amountRules: List<ValueValidatorRule<String>> = listOf(Required, Decimal)

/** Immutable: the text is a String snapshot. The TextFieldState lives on the component, not here. */
data class ExpenseModel(
    val amount: String = "",
    val amountState: FieldValidationState = amountRules.toFieldState("", showError = false),
    val submitAttempts: Int = 0,
) {
    val canSubmit: Boolean get() = listOf(amountState).hasNoErrors()
}

sealed interface ExpenseEvent {
    data class AmountChanged(val text: String) : ExpenseEvent
    data object AmountFocusLost : ExpenseEvent
    data object Submit : ExpenseEvent
}

fun reduce(model: ExpenseModel, event: ExpenseEvent): ExpenseModel = when (event) {
    // Identical in shape to the TextFieldValue hoist: fold on the text, preserve showError.
    is ExpenseEvent.AmountChanged -> model.copy(
        amount = event.text,
        amountState = amountRules.toFieldState(event.text, model.amountState.showError),
    )
    ExpenseEvent.AmountFocusLost ->
        model.copy(amountState = amountRules.toFieldState(model.amount, showError = true))
    ExpenseEvent.Submit -> model.copy(
        amountState = amountRules.toFieldState(model.amount, showError = true),
        submitAttempts = model.submitAttempts + 1,
    )
}

/** The component (Decompose component, ViewModel, presenter…) — NOT the Model. */
@Stable
class ExpenseComponent(scope: CoroutineScope) {
    /** The field's editing buffer. A `val`, created once, never copied into the Model. */
    val amount = TextFieldState()

    var model by mutableStateOf(ExpenseModel())
        private set

    fun dispatch(event: ExpenseEvent) {
        model = reduce(model, event)
    }

    init {
        // state → model: the one-way hand-off. Text only; caret moves don't emit.
        scope.launch { amount.textChanges().collect { dispatch(ExpenseEvent.AmountChanged(it)) } }
    }
}

@Composable
fun ExpenseForm(component: ExpenseComponent) {
    val model = component.model
    OutlinedTextField(
        state = component.amount,
        modifier = Modifier
            .onFocusCursorToEnd(state = component.amount)
            .validationBehavior(
                isError = model.amountState.isError,
                shakeTrigger = model.submitAttempts,
                onFocusLost = { component.dispatch(ExpenseEvent.AmountFocusLost) },
            ),
        isError = model.amountState.isError,
        supportingText = model.amountState.supportingText(),
    )
}

Compared with today. rules.toFieldState(value.text, showError) becomes rules.toFieldState(text, showError), and everything else (keystroke events preserve showError, focus-loss and submit force it, hasNoErrors() for canSubmit, the submitAttempts shake counter) carries over unchanged. The Model's field type shrinks from TextFieldValue to String, because the caret now lives in the TextFieldState. The rules about seeding and clamping TextRange no longer apply.

Caveats.

  • The hand-off is asynchronous: the Model catches up on the next snapshot apply, before the next frame. A click handler runs as a later event and sees the final text. If an action can fire in the same frame as an edit, carry the text in the event: Submit(amount = amount.text.toString()).
  • textChanges() conflates. A burst of edits may arrive as its final text, which is all a reducer needs.
  • Process death: persist the Model's String (it is the source of truth for restore) and re-seed the state from it, or use rememberTextFieldState / TextFieldState.Saver for a UI-owned state.

docs.title: 4. Programmatic writes (suggestion, preset, re-seed, clear)
docs.text:
Write the TextFieldState, never the Model. Writes travel one way: state → Model through textChanges(). setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd puts the caret at the end, which replaces TextFieldValue(text, TextRange(text.length)) helpers such as a "caret-end entry". A new TextFieldState(text) also starts with the caret at the end.

/** A reducer-owned, one-shot write request. The version makes each request distinct. */
data class Seed(val text: String, val version: Int)

@Composable
fun ProgrammaticWrites(state: TextFieldState, suggestions: List<String>, seed: Seed?) {
    // Reducer re-seed (server load, edit prefill): apply only when the version changes, so it can
    // never overwrite keystrokes the Model hasn't caught up with yet.
    LaunchedEffect(seed?.version) {
        if (seed != null) state.setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd(seed.text)
    }
    Column {
        OutlinedTextField(state = state)
        // Suggestion pick / preset fill: write the state at the event's source. Caret lands at the
        // end; the textChanges() collector carries the text to the Model.
        suggestions.forEach { s ->
            Button(onClick = { state.setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd(s) }) { Text(s) }
        }
        // Clear.
        Button(onClick = { state.clearText() }) { Text("Clear") }
    }
}
Write Where it originates How Suggestion pick, preset fill UI event state.setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd(text) in the handler Clear UI event state.clearText() Re-seed (server load, edit prefill, reset after save) Reducer Reducer publishes a versioned Seed(text, version) (or a one-shot effect). The UI applies it in LaunchedEffect(seed.version)

Rejected: the model echo (LaunchedEffect(model.text) { if (state.text != model.text) state.set…(model.text) }). It loses keystrokes. Type "a" and the Model becomes "a". Type "b" before the effect runs, and the effect compares the state's "ab" with the Model's stale "a" and writes "a" back. A versioned seed fires only when the reducer means to write.

With a validator, the write path decides whether it counts as user interaction:

  • validator.value = text: replaces the text, caret at end, not interaction. The field stays pristine, exactly like assigning TextFieldValueValidator.value. Use it for a re-seed, followed by reset() if the field should look untouched.
  • validator.validate(text): replaces the text and shows errors.
  • A write straight to the state (setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd, clearText, edit {}) cannot be told apart from typing, so it is interaction. That is right for a suggestion pick.

docs.title: 5. Transformations: raw or transformed text?
docs.text:
Rules, textChanges() and the Model all see TextFieldState.text:

  • after the InputTransformation. It runs on user edits (typing, paste, IME) and changes what is stored. A digit filter means the validator never sees the rejected characters.
  • before the OutputTransformation. It only changes what is drawn. "12.5" displayed as "12.50" is still "12.5" to the rules.
  • Programmatic writes bypass the InputTransformation. setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd("12a") stores "12a". Normalise a preset before writing it.
/** Input: reject anything but digits and one dot. Rules see the filtered text. */
val CurrencyInput = InputTransformation.byValue { current, proposed ->
    val filtered = proposed.filter { it.isDigit() || it == '.' }
    if (filtered.count { it == '.' } > 1) current else filtered
}

/** Output: display-only "12.5" → "12.50". Rules and the Model still see "12.5". */
val CurrencyDisplay = OutputTransformation {
    val dot = asCharSequence().indexOf('.')
    if (dot >= 0) repeat(2 - (length - dot - 1)) { insert(length, "0") }
}

@Composable
fun CurrencyField(component: ExpenseComponent) {
    val model = component.model
    OutlinedTextField(
        state = component.amount,
        inputTransformation = CurrencyInput,
        outputTransformation = CurrencyDisplay,
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Decimal),
        modifier = Modifier.validationBehavior(
            isError = model.amountState.isError,
            shakeTrigger = model.submitAttempts,
            onFocusLost = { component.dispatch(ExpenseEvent.AmountFocusLost) },
        ),
        isError = model.amountState.isError,
        supportingText = model.amountState.supportingText(),
    )
}

Reshaping like currency "12.5" → "12.50". Don't pad in an InputTransformation: it rewrites stored text on every keystroke, fights the caret, and the user can't delete the digit it keeps re-adding. Use the InputTransformation to restrict (digits, one dot, maxLength). Use an OutputTransformation to present (padding, grouping, a currency symbol). Write rules against the stored, unpadded form. If the stored value itself must be canonical, normalise once on blur with a programmatic write in the focus-lost handler.

docs.title: Deprecation (Compose 1.13+)
docs.text:
Compose 1.13 deprecates BasicTextField(value, onValueChange, …) for both String and TextFieldValue; 1.11 and 1.12 don't. (Checked in the bytecode: in CMP 1.13.0-beta02 and androidx material3 1.5.0-rc01 the material3 TextField/OutlinedTextField value overloads aren't annotated yet, but the foundation field they wrap is.) yakcov follows the same line. Only the 1.13+ artifacts deprecate the wrappers around that shape:

Deprecated in 1.13+ Use instead TextFieldValueValidator TextFieldStateValidator rememberTextFieldValueValidator(value: String, …) rememberTextFieldStateValidator(initialText = …) (IDE quick-fix via ReplaceWith) rememberTextFieldValueValidator(textFieldValue: MutableState<TextFieldValue>, …) rememberTextFieldStateValidator(textFieldState = …) Modifier.onFocusCursorToEnd(value, onValueChange, …) Modifier.onFocusCursorToEnd(state = …) PasswordMatches(textFieldValueField) PasswordMatches(stringField) with a TextFieldStateValidator

The level is warning, so builds keep compiling while you migrate. Nothing is removed; removal comes in a later release. Everything not tied to the deprecated field shape is untouched: ValueValidator, the rules, GenericValueValidator, FieldValidator, FieldValidationState, validationBehavior, shakeOnInvalid and onFocusLost.

How it's built. All channels compile one common source set, and Kotlin rejects a typealias to kotlin.Deprecated. So those declarations carry an internal marker, @TextFieldValueApi(…). Before 1.13 it's a source-only no-op. On 1.13+, the deprecateTextFieldValueApi Gradle task compiles a copy of each file that uses it, with the marker rewritten to @Deprecated(…). File names, JVM facades and the ABI dump don't change.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Validation state (pristine/validating/showing errors) is not saveable. This is the same as TextFieldValueValidator. rememberTextFieldStateValidator does save the text.
  • The pristine → validating step needs the observer running (see §1). Without it, rules still evaluate live, but a fresh field won't start validating until blur or submit.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: TextFieldStateValidatorTest (validator, timing, caret, transformations, textChanges), TextFieldStateUdfTest (state → Model hand-off, programmatic writes, versioned re-seed, the submit-counter shake) and AsyncModelInputTest (fast typing, mid-text paste and a re-seed under an async model, each with a legacy control proving the harness detects the loss) run in full on JVM, Wasm and the iOS simulator. Android unit tests and JS run the pure (non-UI) cases and skip the Compose UI ones, as the rest of the suite does (@AndroidJUnitIgnore / @JSIgnore).

docs.title: Basic screen
docs.text:
When to use: quick forms and screens with no state holder — the validators live directly in the composable.

@Composable
fun BasicSignUpScreen(onSubmit: (email: String, password: String) -> Unit) {
    // No state holder: the validators live in the composable, remembered across
    // recompositions. Each one owns a TextFieldState (the field's text) and validates it by
    // observing the state — there is no onValueChange to wire.
    val email = rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules = listOf(Required, Email))
    val password = rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules = listOf(Required, MinLength(8)))

    Column {
        with(email) {
            OutlinedTextField(
                state = textFieldState,
                label = { Text("Email") },
                isError = isError(),
                supportingText = supportingText(),
                lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .fillMaxWidth()
                    // Show errors when focus leaves the field; shake on invalid submit.
                    .validationConfig(validateOnFocusLost = true, shakeOnInvalid = true),
            )
        }
        with(password) {
            OutlinedTextField(
                state = textFieldState,
                label = { Text("Password") },
                isError = isError(),
                supportingText = supportingText(),
                lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .fillMaxWidth()
                    .validationConfig(validateOnFocusLost = true, shakeOnInvalid = true),
            )
        }
        Button(
            onClick = {
                // Form-level validate(): surfaces errors on every field, true when all pass.
                if (listOf(email, password).validate()) {
                    onSubmit(email.value, password.value)
                }
            },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        ) { Text("Create account") }
    }
}

How the wiring works:

  • rememberTextFieldStateValidator keeps each validator across recompositions. It owns the field's TextFieldState (the text, saved across configuration change) and its validation state, and it validates by observing the state, so there's no onValueChange to wire. The older rememberTextFieldValueValidator (value/onValueChange) still works.
  • Modifier.validationConfig(validateOnFocusLost = true, shakeOnInvalid = true) starts validation when the user leaves the field and shakes it when a submit finds it invalid. Nothing turns red while they're still typing.
  • The submit button gates on listOf(email, password).validate() — this surfaces errors on every field (including ones the user never touched) and returns true only when all rules pass.

When the form grows a real state holder, graduate to the ViewModel, MVI, or Circuit wiring.

docs.title: Circuit
docs.text: Recommended wiring: the presenter owns each field's TextFieldState and the validator that follows it. Circuit presenters are composable functions, so remember { TextFieldState() }, remember { FieldValidator(...) } and a LaunchedEffect that pipes textChanges() into the validator all work there naturally. The field owns the text, the presenter owns the form state, and the UI stays a dumb renderer of CircuitUiState. The text is never rendered from state, so a late recomposition can't drop a keystroke (see the decision record).

docs.title: State and events
docs.text:
/**
 * Circuit state. Each field contributes its editing buffer (a TextFieldState — the field owns the
 * text) and the FieldValidator that follows it; both are @Stable references. Events flow back via
 * the sink.
 */
data class SignUpState(
    val emailText: TextFieldState,
    val email: FieldValidator<String>,
    val passwordText: TextFieldState,
    val password: FieldValidator<String>,
    val submitted: Boolean?,
    val eventSink: (SignUpEvent) -> Unit,
) : CircuitUiState

sealed interface SignUpEvent : CircuitUiEvent {
    data object Submit : SignUpEvent
}

docs.title: The presenter
docs.text:
class SignUpPresenter : Presenter<SignUpState> {
    @Composable
    override fun present(): SignUpState {
        // Circuit presenters are composable functions, so `remember` keeps the text buffers and
        // validators across recompositions (`rememberRetained` to survive Circuit's retention).
        val emailText = remember { TextFieldState() }
        val passwordText = remember { TextFieldState() }
        val email = remember { FieldValidator("", rules = listOf(Required, Email)) }
        val password = remember { FieldValidator("", rules = listOf(Required, MinLength(8))) }
        // One-way hand-off: the field's text -> its validator. Never the other way.
        LaunchedEffect(emailText) { emailText.textChanges().collect(email::onValueChange) }
        LaunchedEffect(passwordText) { passwordText.textChanges().collect(password::onValueChange) }
        var submitted by remember { mutableStateOf<Boolean?>(null) }
        return SignUpState(emailText, email, passwordText, password, submitted) { event ->
            when (event) {
                // Form-level validate(): shows errors on every field, true when all pass.
                SignUpEvent.Submit -> submitted = listOf(email, password).validate()
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: The UI
docs.text:
@Composable
fun SignUpUi(state: SignUpState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    Column(modifier) {
        ValidatedField(state.emailText, state.email, label = "Email")
        ValidatedField(state.passwordText, state.password, label = "Password")
        Button(
            onClick = { state.eventSink(SignUpEvent.Submit) },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        ) { Text("Create account") }
        state.submitted?.let { Text(if (it) "Valid — proceeding" else "Fix the errors above") }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ValidatedField(text: TextFieldState, field: FieldValidator<String>, label: String) {
    OutlinedTextField(
        state = text, // the field owns the text — no value / onValueChange
        label = { Text(label) },
        isError = field.state.isError,
        supportingText = field.state.supportingText(),
        lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .onFocusLost { field.onFocusLost() },
    )
}

docs.title: Hosting it
docs.text:
/**
 * Minimal host. In a real app you register SignUpPresenter/SignUpUi in a Circuit via
 * Presenter.Factory + Ui.Factory and render through CircuitContent(screen); a routed
 * Screen needs @Parcelize on Android, which is app-level wiring beyond validation —
 * so we keep it out of this example.
 */
@Composable
fun SignUpCircuitHost() {
    val presenter = remember { SignUpPresenter() }
    SignUpUi(presenter.present())
}

What this example leaves out

A real app routes via a Screen + CircuitContent, registering the presenter and UI through Presenter.Factory / Ui.Factory. Screen is Parcelable on Android (@Parcelize plumbing), which is app-level wiring unrelated to validation — so the example hosts the presenter directly. Only circuit-foundation is needed for everything shown here, and rememberRetained is a drop-in upgrade for remember if you want the text buffers and validators to survive Circuit's retention scope.

Prefer immutable state throughout? The MVI/UDF wiring drops into a Circuit presenter unchanged. Fold rules with toFieldState, put the text String and the FieldValidationState in your CircuitUiState instead of the validator, and keep the TextFieldState in the presenter.

docs.title: MVI / UDF
docs.text:
Recommended wiring: the field owns a TextFieldState, the Model observes it. A reducer's contract is (Model, Event) -> Model with an immutable Model. The text being typed must not round-trip through that Model, because a Model update that lands after the next key resets the field and drops the keystroke or misplaces a paste. Instead:

  • each field owns a TextFieldState (the editing buffer, on the Compose clock), held by your component, never by the Model;
  • the Model holds each field's text as a plain String plus its immutable FieldValidationState;
  • the reducer folds rules with the pure toFieldState(text, showError), exactly as before.

Text flows one way: field → textChanges() → dispatch → reduce. See the TextFieldState decision record for why, including a side-by-side demo of the old shape losing input.

Compose versions

TextFieldState exists on every Compose line yakcov ships (1.11+). Compose 1.13 deprecates the value/onValueChange text fields this replaces, so new forms should start here.

docs.title: 1. Model and events
docs.text:
The Model holds text as a String, not a TextFieldValue or a TextFieldState. The caret and selection live in the field's TextFieldState, so the Model doesn't need them.

// Plain top-level rule lists: shared by reduce() and any unit test, no Compose needed.
private val emailRules: List<ValueValidatorRule<String>> = listOf(Required, Email)
private val passwordRules: List<ValueValidatorRule<String>> = listOf(Required, MinLength(8))

// Every field is a val; FieldValidationState is @Immutable, so the Model is value-stable.
data class SignUpModel(
    val email: String = "",
    val emailState: FieldValidationState = FieldValidationState.Pristine,
    val password: String = "",
    val passwordState: FieldValidationState = FieldValidationState.Pristine,
    /** null = not attempted, true = accepted, false = blocked (errors surfaced). */
    val submitted: Boolean? = null,
    /** Monotonic submit counter — drives shake. A repeated invalid submit yields an
     *  EQUAL FieldValidationState, so a state diff alone can never re-fire the shake. */
    val submitAttempts: Int = 0,
) {
    /** Driven purely by severity (ignores showError) — live from the first frame. */
    val canSubmit: Boolean get() = listOf(emailState, passwordState).hasNoErrors()
}

/** Seed with rules pre-run (showError = false) so canSubmit is honest before any input. */
fun initialSignUpModel(): SignUpModel = SignUpModel(
    emailState = emailRules.toFieldState("", showError = false),
    passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState("", showError = false),
)

sealed interface SignUpEvent {
    data class EmailChanged(val value: String) : SignUpEvent
    data object EmailFocusLost : SignUpEvent
    data class PasswordChanged(val value: String) : SignUpEvent
    data object PasswordFocusLost : SignUpEvent
    data object Submit : SignUpEvent
}

docs.title: 2. The reducer
docs.text:
Plain Kotlin, unit-testable, and unchanged from the pre-TextFieldState shape: a Changed event carries the new text and preserves showError, while FocusLost/Submit force it to true.

// THE pure core: (Model, Event) -> Model. No Compose, no coroutines, no IO.
// showError is threaded, not recomputed: Changed preserves it; FocusLost/Submit force it true.
fun reduce(model: SignUpModel, event: SignUpEvent): SignUpModel = when (event) {
    is SignUpEvent.EmailChanged -> model.copy(
        email = event.value,
        emailState = emailRules.toFieldState(event.value, model.emailState.showError),
        submitted = null,
    )
    SignUpEvent.EmailFocusLost -> model.copy(
        emailState = emailRules.toFieldState(model.email, showError = true),
    )
    is SignUpEvent.PasswordChanged -> model.copy(
        password = event.value,
        passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState(event.value, model.passwordState.showError),
        submitted = null,
    )
    SignUpEvent.PasswordFocusLost -> model.copy(
        passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState(model.password, showError = true),
    )
    SignUpEvent.Submit -> {
        // Surface errors on every field, then read validity off severity.
        val surfaced = model.copy(
            emailState = emailRules.toFieldState(model.email, showError = true),
            passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState(model.password, showError = true),
            submitAttempts = model.submitAttempts + 1,
        )
        surfaced.copy(submitted = surfaced.canSubmit)
    }
}

docs.title: 3. The component owns the TextFieldStates and pipes their text into the store
docs.text:
This is the only new piece. Create one TextFieldState per field once, as a val on the component (a ViewModel, a Decompose component, a presenter). Then collect textChanges() into dispatch.

// The component: your ViewModel / Decompose component / presenter. It owns two things:
//  - the store (Model + dispatch) — the source of truth for everything except the keystrokes, and
//  - one TextFieldState per field — the editing buffer, owned by the field on the Compose clock.
// Text flows ONE way: field -> textChanges() -> dispatch -> reduce. Nothing ever writes the Model
// back into a field while the user types, so no keystroke or paste can be lost to a late update.
@Stable
class SignUpComponent(scope: CoroutineScope, initial: SignUpModel = initialSignUpModel()) {
    val email = TextFieldState(initial.email)
    val password = TextFieldState(initial.password)

    var model by mutableStateOf(initial)
        private set

    fun dispatch(event: SignUpEvent) {
        model = reduce(model, event)
    }

    init {
        // The whole hand-off. textChanges() emits plain Strings (current text first, then each
        // change) and ignores caret moves. In a ViewModel pass viewModelScope; in Decompose, the
        // component's lifecycle scope.
        scope.launch { email.textChanges().collect { dispatch(SignUpEvent.EmailChanged(it)) } }
        scope.launch { password.textChanges().collect { dispatch(SignUpEvent.PasswordChanged(it)) } }
    }
}

docs.title: 4. Bind the UI
docs.text:
Pass state = to the field. There is no value/onValueChange. Errors, supporting text, shake and focus-loss come from the Model, exactly as before.

@Composable
fun MviSignUpScreen() {
    // In an app this is your ViewModel / component; remembered here to keep the example standalone.
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    val component = remember { SignUpComponent(scope) }
    val model = component.model
    Column {
        OutlinedTextField(
            state = component.email, // the field owns the text — no value / onValueChange
            label = { Text("Email") },
            isError = model.emailState.isError,
            supportingText = model.emailState.supportingText(),
            lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxWidth()
                .onFocusCursorToEnd(state = component.email)
                .validationBehavior(
                    isError = model.emailState.isError,
                    shakeTrigger = model.submitAttempts,
                    onFocusLost = { component.dispatch(SignUpEvent.EmailFocusLost) },
                ),
        )
        OutlinedTextField(
            state = component.password,
            label = { Text("Password") },
            isError = model.passwordState.isError,
            supportingText = model.passwordState.supportingText(),
            lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxWidth()
                .validationBehavior(
                    isError = model.passwordState.isError,
                    shakeTrigger = model.submitAttempts,
                    onFocusLost = { component.dispatch(SignUpEvent.PasswordFocusLost) },
                ),
        )
        Button(
            onClick = { component.dispatch(SignUpEvent.Submit) },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        ) { Text(if (model.canSubmit) "Create account" else "Fix errors to submit") }
        model.submitted?.let { Text(if (it) "Valid — proceeding" else "Fix the errors above") }
    }
}

docs.title: 5. Programmatic writes
docs.text:
Write to the TextFieldState, never to the Model. The write travels the same path as typing, and the Model catches up through textChanges(). setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd leaves the caret at the end, so there's no TextRange bookkeeping.

// Programmatic writes (suggestion pick, prefill, clear) go to the TextFieldState — the same path as
// typing — and reach the Model through textChanges(). The caret lands at the end.
fun SignUpComponent.prefillEmail(suggestion: String) = email.setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd(suggestion)

fun SignUpComponent.clearForm() {
    email.clearText()
    password.clearText()
}

When the reducer decides the text, for example a server load or a template fill, it can't touch the state because it's pure. Have it publish a one-shot, versioned seed, and apply that seed only when its version changes:

/** A reducer-owned, one-shot write request. The version makes each request distinct. */
data class Seed(val text: String, val version: Int)

@Composable
fun ProgrammaticWrites(state: TextFieldState, suggestions: List<String>, seed: Seed?) {
    // Reducer re-seed (server load, edit prefill): apply only when the version changes, so it can
    // never overwrite keystrokes the Model hasn't caught up with yet.
    LaunchedEffect(seed?.version) {
        if (seed != null) state.setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd(seed.text)
    }
    Column {
        OutlinedTextField(state = state)
        // Suggestion pick / preset fill: write the state at the event's source. Caret lands at the
        // end; the textChanges() collector carries the text to the Model.
        suggestions.forEach { s ->
            Button(onClick = { state.setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd(s) }) { Text(s) }
        }
        // Clear.
        Button(onClick = { state.clearText() }) { Text("Clear") }
    }
}

docs.title: Rules of the road
docs.text:
• Never put a TextFieldState in the Model. It's a mutable, reference-identity holder, so copy() aliases it and == becomes identity. It lives on the component, like any other UI-owned state.
  • Never echo the Model back into a field. For example, LaunchedEffect(model.email) { email.setText…(model.email) } compares the field against a Model that is one update behind and overwrites the newest keystrokes. Use the versioned seed above.
  • showError is threaded, not recomputed. Changed preserves it, and FocusLost and Submit force it to true. That gives "errors on blur or submit, never mid-keystroke".
  • canSubmit is honest from the first frame. Seed each field with rules.toFieldState("", showError = false), not FieldValidationState.Pristine. hasNoErrors() reads severity and ignores showError.
  • An action in the same frame as an edit: the Model catches up on the next snapshot apply, before the next frame, so a click sees the final text. If something can fire on the very frame of an edit, carry the text in the event: Submit(email = component.email.text.toString()).
  • Formatting goes in inputTransformation (to restrict input) and outputTransformation (to display it differently). Rules see the stored text: after the input transformation and before the output one. See the decision record.
  • Shake is driven by a monotonic counter, not a state diff. FieldValidationState equality includes its message, so a second invalid submit produces an == state, nothing recomposes, and a diff-driven shake would fire only once. Thread a submitAttempts counter in the Model and pass it as shakeTrigger. Modifier.validationBehavior(isError, shakeTrigger, onFocusLost) bundles that with focus-loss handling.
  • Screen readers get no signal from shake. It's a purely visual graphicsLayer translation, so if the form must be accessible, announce a blocked submit yourself.
  • Give disposable fields a stable key. The "don't shake on first frame" guard remembers the trigger it was born with. A field re-created after its subtree was disposed adopts the current counter as its baseline and swallows a shake that fell due while it was gone.
  • Cross-field rules (confirm-password and the like) are SAM lambdas that close over the Model. See custom rules.

docs.title: Migrating from value / onValueChange
docs.text: Before After Model holds TextFieldValue (or String) and the field renders it Model holds String; the component holds a TextFieldState OutlinedTextField(value = model.x, onValueChange = { dispatch(XChanged(it)) }) OutlinedTextField(state = component.x) plus x.textChanges().collect { dispatch(XChanged(it)) } on the component XChanged(value: TextFieldValue), folding on value.text XChanged(text: String), folding on text; the reducer is otherwise unchanged Prefill: TextFieldValue(text, TextRange(text.length)) TextFieldState(text) (caret at the end) or state.setTextAndPlaceCursorAtEnd(text) Filter keystrokes in onValueChange and clamp the caret inputTransformation = …; the caret is handled for you VisualTransformation outputTransformation = … onFocusCursorToEnd(value, onValueChange) onFocusCursorToEnd(state = component.x) validationBehavior(...) unchanged

docs.title: Persistence & process death
docs.text: FieldValidationState is @Immutable @Serializable: severity and showError persist, while the message (result) is @Transient and gets recomputed. The Model's Strings are the source of truth for restore. Persist them with each field's showError, then rehydrate by re-running the rules through toFieldState, and construct the component's TextFieldStates from the restored text (SignUpComponent(scope, initial = restored) does both). For cross-process JSON, add a kotlinx-serialization runtime and encode FieldValidationState directly. It persists Outcome by constant name.

docs.title: ViewModel
docs.text:
Recommended wiring: the field owns a TextFieldState, and the validator lives in the ViewModel and follows it. The VM holds one TextFieldState per field (the editing buffer) and a FieldValidator per field. textChanges() feeds the text to the validator, one way. FieldValidator has a plain constructor and is snapshot-state backed, so the form state survives configuration changes, submit() is unit-testable with no Compose UI, and composables reading field.state recompose automatically.

If your team's convention is strictly-immutable UI state, the second tab keeps a pure UiState of Strings and FieldValidationStates, fed the same way.

Don't render the text from VM state

OutlinedTextField(value = state.email, onValueChange = vm::onEmailChange) with a StateFlow + collectAsState() is the textbook skipped-input setup. collectAsState() delivers on a later frame, the field is reset to the stale text, and fast typing or a paste loses characters. Compose 1.13 deprecates that text-field shape. Let the field own the text, and have the VM observe it. See the decision record.

Validator in the ViewModel (recommended)Immutable UiState 
class SignUpViewModel : ViewModel() {
    // The FIELD owns the text: one TextFieldState per field, created once with the VM (so the
    // draft survives configuration changes). Never round-trip the text through the VM's state.
    val emailText = TextFieldState()
    val passwordText = TextFieldState()

    // FieldValidator has a plain (non-@Composable) constructor, so it is safe to own in a
    // ViewModel. Here it FOLLOWS the field's text and owns the validation state.
    val email = FieldValidator("", rules = listOf(Required, Email))
    val password = FieldValidator("", rules = listOf(Required, MinLength(8)))

    init {
        // One-way hand-off: text -> validator. textChanges() emits Strings and ignores caret moves.
        viewModelScope.launch { emailText.textChanges().collect(email::onValueChange) }
        viewModelScope.launch { passwordText.textChanges().collect(password::onValueChange) }
    }

    /** Form-level submit: shows errors on every field, true when all pass. Unit-testable without UI. */
    fun submit(): Boolean = listOf(email, password).validate()
}

@Composable
fun SignUpScreen(
    onSubmit: () -> Unit,
    viewModel: SignUpViewModel = viewModel { SignUpViewModel() },
) {
    Column {
        ValidatedField(viewModel.emailText, viewModel.email, label = "Email")
        ValidatedField(viewModel.passwordText, viewModel.password, label = "Password")
        Button(
            // submit() surfaces errors on every field and returns true only when all pass.
            onClick = { if (viewModel.submit()) onSubmit() },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        ) { Text("Create account") }
    }
}

// The @Composable rendering helpers are called HERE, in composition — never in the
// ViewModel. isError is a plain property; supportingText() resolves string resources.
@Composable
private fun ValidatedField(text: TextFieldState, field: FieldValidator<String>, label: String) {
    OutlinedTextField(
        state = text, // the field owns the text — no value / onValueChange
        label = { Text(label) },
        isError = field.state.isError,
        supportingText = field.state.supportingText(),
        lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .onFocusLost { field.onFocusLost() },
    )
}

private val emailRules = listOf(Required, Email)
private val passwordRules = listOf(Required, MinLength(8))

/** Text is a plain String snapshot of the field; the caret lives in the field's TextFieldState. */
data class SignUpUiState(
    val email: String = "",
    val emailState: FieldValidationState = FieldValidationState.Pristine,
    val password: String = "",
    val passwordState: FieldValidationState = FieldValidationState.Pristine,
) {
    val canSubmit: Boolean get() = listOf(emailState, passwordState).hasNoErrors()
}

class HoistedSignUpViewModel : ViewModel() {
    // The editing buffers — on the VM, NOT in SignUpUiState.
    val emailText = TextFieldState()
    val passwordText = TextFieldState()

    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(
        // Seed by folding the rules with showError = false so canSubmit is honest
        // before any input (a pristine required field must not look submittable).
        SignUpUiState(
            emailState = emailRules.toFieldState("", showError = false),
            passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState("", showError = false),
        )
    )
    val state: StateFlow<SignUpUiState> = _state.asStateFlow()

    init {
        // field -> UiState, one way. The UiState never flows back into the field, so a state
        // update that lands a frame late can't overwrite (and drop) a newer keystroke.
        viewModelScope.launch { emailText.textChanges().collect(::onEmailChange) }
        viewModelScope.launch { passwordText.textChanges().collect(::onPasswordChange) }
    }

    private fun onEmailChange(value: String) = _state.update {
        // Recompute severity on every keystroke, but PRESERVE showError so no
        // error pops while the user is still typing.
        it.copy(email = value, emailState = emailRules.toFieldState(value, it.emailState.showError))
    }

    fun onEmailFocusLost() = _state.update {
        it.copy(emailState = emailRules.toFieldState(it.email, showError = true))
    }

    private fun onPasswordChange(value: String) = _state.update {
        it.copy(password = value, passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState(value, it.passwordState.showError))
    }

    fun onPasswordFocusLost() = _state.update {
        it.copy(passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState(it.password, showError = true))
    }

    /** Submit: force errors visible on all fields, then read validity off severity. */
    fun submit(): Boolean = _state.updateAndGet {
        it.copy(
            emailState = emailRules.toFieldState(it.email, showError = true),
            passwordState = passwordRules.toFieldState(it.password, showError = true),
        )
    }.canSubmit
}

@Composable
fun HoistedSignUpScreen(
    viewModel: HoistedSignUpViewModel = viewModel { HoistedSignUpViewModel() },
) {
    val state by viewModel.state.collectAsState()
    Column {
        OutlinedTextField(
            state = viewModel.emailText,
            label = { Text("Email") },
            isError = state.emailState.isError,
            supportingText = state.emailState.supportingText(),
            lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxWidth()
                .onFocusLost(viewModel::onEmailFocusLost),
        )
        OutlinedTextField(
            state = viewModel.passwordText,
            label = { Text("Password") },
            isError = state.passwordState.isError,
            supportingText = state.passwordState.supportingText(),
            lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxWidth()
                .onFocusLost(viewModel::onPasswordFocusLost),
        )
        Button(
            onClick = { viewModel.submit() },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        ) { Text(if (state.canSubmit) "Create account" else "Fix errors to submit") }
    }
}

The @Composable boundary

The ViewModel never calls the @Composable rendering helpers. field.state.isError is a plain property the VM can read; supportingText() resolves string resources and must be called from the UI, in composition. Keep severity logic in the state holder and rendering in the composable.

Construct once, never copy

Construct a FieldValidator once and hold it (a VM/presenter field, DI, or remember). Don't construct it inside a recomposing body and don't copy it — both reset its validation state.

Formatting fields

Fields that reformat as the user types (currency, phone) use inputTransformation to restrict input and outputTransformation to change how it's displayed. The TextFieldState keeps the caret right, and the validator sees the stored text (after the input transformation, before the output one). There's no TextFieldValue or caret clamping to hand-roll. See Transformations.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
FieldValidator takes an optional observer — a FieldValidatorObserver fired after every mutation commits (ValueChanged / Validated / Reset) with the post-mutation value + state. Handy for analytics, logging, or driving UI like the sample's live state-flow visualizer (StateFlowSample.kt). No event fires at construction; observers must not throw.

On restore-from-persistence, prefer FieldValidator(initial = restoredDraft, rules, initialValidate = true) over calling validate() — it re-runs the rules without emitting a Validated event an analytics tap would over-count.

Unit-testing presenters

If presenter/VM unit tests construct FieldValidator or read .value/.state, add org.jetbrains.compose:runtime to the test source set — it is not pulled in transitively.

docs.title: Built-in rules
docs.text:
Yakcov ships rules for the common cases so you rarely have to write your own. Every rule implements ValueValidatorRule<V>; drop them into a validator's rules list. To write your own, see custom rules.

Blank / null pass through

The string format rules treat blank input as valid (MinLength included), and the value-membership/bounds generic rules (InList, Min, Max, InRange) treat null as valid — so Required (or generic Required) is the single source of presence-checking. Compose it alongside the rule whenever an empty field should be rejected: listOf(Email) accepts an empty field, listOf(Required, Email) doesn't. The presence/state checks (Required, ListNotEmpty, IsChecked) and the date-part rules (DayValidation/MonthValidation/YearValidation, which need a value to parse) are the exceptions — they reject blank/null.

docs.title: String rules
docs.text:
com.chrisjenx.yakcov.strings — validate the text of a TextField (rememberTextFieldValueValidator).

Rule Passes when Required the value is not blank Email the value is a valid email address Phone(region) a valid phone number for an ISO region — needs libphonenumber, see phone validation PhoneFormat the value looks like a phone number — lenient, no extra dependency Numeric the value parses as a whole number Decimal the value parses as a decimal MinValue(n) / MaxValue(n) the parsed numeric value is >= n / <= n MinLength(n) / MaxLength(n) the length is within bounds (MinLength can trim and exclude whitespace) HexColor a CSS hex color: #RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (case-insensitive) OneOf(allowed) the value is one of a Set<String> — trims and ignores case by default (ignoreCase / trim flags) DayValidation / MonthValidation / YearValidation the day/month/year part forms a valid date (given a sibling LocalDate) PasswordMatches(other) the value equals another field's value

docs.title: Generic rules
docs.text:
com.chrisjenx.yakcov.generic — validate a typed value T directly, with rememberGenericValueValidator(state, rules).

Rule Passes when Required<T>() the value is not null InList(allowed) the value is one of allowed (null passes) ListNotEmpty() the List value is non-empty IsChecked / IsNotChecked a Boolean? is / isn't true Min(n) / Max(n) / InRange(min, max) a numeric N? where N : Number, Comparable is in range — null and NaN pass

The typed numeric bounds complement the string-based MinValue/MaxValue for fields whose value is already numeric. Because they pass null through, the validator's value type must be nullable (e.g. Int?):

@Composable
fun QuantityField() {
    // Typed numeric bounds validate the value directly (no string parsing). null and NaN
    // pass — pair with generic Required for presence. The value type must be nullable
    // (Int?) so the bounds' null pass-through type-checks.
    val quantity = rememberGenericValueValidator<Int?>(
        state = 1,
        rules = listOf(Min(1), Max(99)),
    )
    Text(if (quantity.isValid) "OK" else "Enter 1–99")
}

docs.title: Conditional rules
docs.text:
onlyWhen (and the underlying Optional) wrap any rule — string or generic — so it runs only while a State<Boolean> is true, and passes otherwise. Use it for conditionally-required or optional-when-hidden fields instead of writing a bespoke variant:

// onlyWhen wraps any rule so it runs only while a State<Boolean> is true; otherwise the
// value passes. Collapses conditionally-required / optional-when-hidden fields into the
// existing rules instead of a bespoke rule per case.
fun taxIdRules(isBusiness: State<Boolean>): List<ValueValidatorRule<String>> =
    listOf(Required.onlyWhen(isBusiness), MinLength(9).onlyWhen(isBusiness))

For "optional, but at least N chars if the user types something", gate only Required and leave the length rule ungated — Required.onlyWhen(state) owns the empty case while the ungated MinLength still enforces length once a value is typed (because blank always passes through to Required):

// "Optional, but at least N chars if the user types something." Gate only Required by the
// state; leave MinLength ungated. Required.onlyWhen owns the empty case (blank passes when
// not required), while the ungated MinLength still rejects a too-short value once typed —
// because every string rule treats blank as valid and defers emptiness to Required.
fun nicknameRules(required: State<Boolean>): List<ValueValidatorRule<String>> =
    listOf(Required.onlyWhen(required), MinLength(3))

docs.title: Severities
docs.text: Rules aren't limited to pass/fail. ValidationResult.outcome() is ranked ERROR > WARNING > INFO > SUCCESS; only ERROR blocks validate()/submission, while warnings and info still surface through supportingText. See custom rules for grading your own.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text: A rule is anything implementing ValueValidatorRule<V> — return a ValidationResult from validate(value). For the rules that already ship, see built-in rules; to run an existing rule only sometimes, see onlyWhen.

docs.title: Reusable rule types
docs.text:
// A reusable rule: an object (or data class for parameterised rules) implementing
// ValueValidatorRule<V>. Return success for blank input — let Required own emptiness.
data object UsZipCode : ValueValidatorRule<String> {
    private val zip = Regex("""^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$""")
    override fun validate(value: String): ValidationResult {
        if (value.isBlank()) return RegularValidationResult.success()
        return if (zip.matches(value)) RegularValidationResult.success()
        else RegularValidationResult.error("Enter a valid ZIP code")
    }
}

Use a data class instead of data object when the rule takes parameters (MinLength(minLength = 8) is built that way).

docs.title: One-off rules (SAM lambdas)
docs.text:
// ValueValidatorRule is a fun interface — one-off rules can be inline SAM lambdas.
// Severity is graded: error/warning/info/success all flow through supportingText.
val NoPlusAddressing = ValueValidatorRule<String> { value ->
    if ("+" in value) RegularValidationResult.warning("Plus-addressing may break receipts")
    else RegularValidationResult.success()
}

docs.title: Severities and results
docs.text:
ValidationResult.outcome() ranks ERROR > WARNING > INFO > SUCCESS. Only ERROR blocks validate()/submission — warnings and info messages display through supportingText without failing the field.

Two result implementations ship with the library:

  • RegularValidationResult.error/warning/info/success("message") — plain strings, shown verbatim
  • ResourceValidationResult — backed by Compose StringResource for i18n; all the built-in rules use this

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Return success for blank input and let Required own emptiness — that way every rule composes with optional fields (listOf(UsZipCode) allows blank, listOf(Required, UsZipCode) doesn't).
  • Rules run on every value change; keep validate cheap and side-effect free.

docs.title: Phone validation
docs.text:
Yakcov ships two phone rules. Pick based on whether you need the libphonenumber dependency:

Rule Dependency Checks PhoneFormat none Lenient "looks like a phone number" format gate: optional leading +, digits and ( ) . / - separators, 7–15 digits. Phone libphonenumber-kotlin (compileOnly) Region-aware validity via Google's libphonenumber.

docs.title: Default: PhoneFormat (no setup)
docs.text:
PhoneFormat has no dependencies and runs on every target. Use it when the server is authoritative (normalizes to E.164 / verifies with a provider, e.g. Telnyx Verify) and the client only needs a cheap format gate:

@Composable
fun PhoneFormatField() {
    // PhoneFormat is a lenient, dependency-free format check — no libphonenumber needed.
    // The server stays authoritative and normalizes to E.164.
    val phone = rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules = listOf(Required, PhoneFormat))
    with(phone) {
        OutlinedTextField(
            state = textFieldState,
            label = { Text("Phone") },
            isError = isError(),
            supportingText = supportingText(),
            lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxWidth()
                .validationConfig(validateOnFocusLost = true),
        )
    }
}

It deliberately accepts a wide range of real-world formats (international +, IDD 00/011 prefixes, national trunk 0, spaces/dashes/dots/parens) and leaves authoritative checks to the server. It does not reject wrong-region or structurally-invalid-but-well-formed numbers — that's Phone's job. The underlying check is also available directly as the public String?.isPhoneNumberFormat() helper.

docs.title: Region-aware: Phone (opt-in)
docs.text:
Phone validates with libphonenumber-kotlin (luca992's multiplatform port of Google's libphonenumber). Yakcov declares it compileOnly, so this rule needs your app (or shared module) to provide the dependency:

commonMain {
    dependencies {
        implementation("io.github.luca992.libphonenumber-kotlin:libphonenumber:0.1.9")
    }
}

@Composable
fun PhoneField() {
    // Phone(defaultRegion) is powered by libphonenumber-kotlin, which yakcov declares
    // compileOnly — your app must add the dependency (see this page's install section).
    val phone = rememberTextFieldStateValidator(rules = listOf(Required, Phone("US")))
    with(phone) {
        OutlinedTextField(
            state = textFieldState,
            label = { Text("Phone") },
            isError = isError(),
            supportingText = supportingText(),
            lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxWidth()
                .validationConfig(validateOnFocusLost = true),
        )
    }
}

Phone also accepts a State<String> for the region, so the default region can react to a country picker: Phone(defaultRegion = countryState).

Without the dependency, using Phone fails at runtime with a missing-class error — everything else in Yakcov (including PhoneFormat) works without it.

docs.title: Testing Phone on Android
docs.text:
In an Android local unit test (plain JVM or Robolectric) Phone reports every number invalid until you configure it. On Android the PhoneNumberUtil is built from an application Context captured by an androidx.startup provider, and libphonenumber reads its metadata through compose-resources — a local unit test creates neither ContentProvider (robolectric#9603, CMP-6612).

This fails silently: isPhoneNumber degrades to false rather than throwing, so assertFalse("abc".isPhoneNumber()) passes whether or not validation actually works, while the positive path is never exercised. One call fixes it:

class PhoneFieldTest {
    @Before fun setUp() = initPhoneNumberUtilForTest()
    @After fun tearDown() = resetPhoneNumberUtilForTest()

    @Test fun acceptsAFrenchNumber() {
        assertTrue("+33 1 42 68 53 00".isPhoneNumber("FR"))
    }
}

initPhoneNumberUtilForTest() needs no Context and loads libphonenumber's real metadata, so every region validates. It only requires that your module keeps Android resources available to unit tests — which is also what Robolectric needs:

android { testOptions { unitTests { isIncludeAndroidResources = true } } }

Call resetPhoneNumberUtilForTest() from @After. The util is a per-JVM singleton, so without it a configured test class silently decides whether a later class that forgot to configure passes — making a suite's result depend on execution order within the shard.

To manage metadata loading yourself, pass your own instance: initPhoneNumberUtilForTest(PhoneNumberUtil.createInstance(myLoader)).

Other targets need no setup: JVM, iOS, JS and WasmJS resolve metadata without a Context. Android instrumented tests need no setup either, since androidx.startup runs there.

docs.title: Roll your own
docs.text: Need a specific national format or an extension field? Write a ValueValidatorRule<String> — see custom rules. The dependency-free String?.isPhoneNumberFormat() helper is public and reusable as a building block.
